name: Seppa
description: District headquarters of East Kameng, situated on the banks of the Kameng River at about 363 m elevation. Scenic valley town with riverside views, local Nyishi markets, and a base for exploring the three valleys and nearby hill stations. Formerly known as Sepla meaning marshy land.
facts: Helipad in the heart of town

name: Bameng
description: Cool hill station and circle headquarters about 48 km north of Seppa. Offers panoramic views of valleys, traditional Nyishi villages, and sight of the snow-peaked Gorichaan mountain. Ideal for quiet escapes amid misty hills and agricultural landscapes.
facts: Cool climate like a hill station

name: Chayangtajo
description: Scenic high-altitude hill station and circle HQ about 81 km from Seppa, famous for views of the snow-peaked Gorichaan mountain. Features cardamom plantations, rice terraces, mountain streams, and authentic Nyishi longhouses in a misty valley setting at around 1,500 m.
facts: Famous for Gorichaan snow peak views

name: Pappu Valley (Lumdung)
description: Spectacular valley along the meandering Pappu River about 21 km from Seppa, named for its snake-like curvy streams. Vast paddy fields, green summer landscapes, and famous for migratory birds in winter at Lumdung. Promoted for eco-tourism including potential paragliding.
facts: Meandering Pappu River with paddy fields
Lumdung known for winter migratory birds
Part of the Three Valleys attraction

name: Kameng River (Seppa section)
description: Major river flowing through East Kameng, popular for angling and fishing in winter near Seppa (permission required from district administration). Offers scenic river views, potential white-water rafting in gorges, and forms the lifeline of the district with turquoise waters amid hills.
facts: Good angling spot in winter with permit

name: Khenewa
description: Scenic valley and circle area with verdant hills, river views, and open spaces. Misty winters add to the beauty; popular for landscape photography, peaceful walks, and local markets amid Nyishi cultural settings. Offbeat stop near Bameng.
facts: Ideal for photography and quiet exploration

name: Lada
description: Remote mountain settlement in the western part of the district, embraced by forests, steep hills, and babbling brooks. Offers peace, privacy, and tribal traditions with pristine landscapes suitable for trekking and photography away from main circuits.

name: Gorichaan Viewpoint (from Bameng/Chayangtajo)
description: Snow-peaked mountain visible from Bameng and Chayangtajo hill stations in East Kameng. Locally significant and a highlight of the area’s high-altitude scenery; best viewed on clear days from elevated points in the district.
facts: Best on clear winter or post-monsoon days

name: Tawang Monastery (Galden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: India’s largest Buddhist monastery and one of the largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Overlooks the Tawang Chu valley with golden roofs, giant Buddha statue, ancient manuscripts, and a living monastic community of hundreds of monks. Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama; major Gelugpa pilgrimage site.

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at about 4170 m (13,700 ft) on the Tawang–West Kameng border, the traditional gateway to Tawang. Features snow-covered landscapes, Sela Lake (Paradise Lake) that often freezes, and panoramic Himalayan views. Now supplemented by the all-weather Sela Tunnel.
facts: Border of Tawang and West Kameng

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake formed by a 1950s earthquake landslide, famous for dead tree trunks rising from turquoise waters. Located on the road toward Bum La Pass; popularly called Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood song sequence filmed here. Army permit often required for access.

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls)
description: Spectacular ~100 m high waterfall near Jang town on the Tawang road, fed by the Nuranang Chu from Sela slopes. Dramatic drop amid green hills; small hydel plant at base. Popular stop on the way to Tawang.
facts: Named after local Monpa girl Nura

name: Bum La Pass
description: High border pass at about 4600 m (15,200 ft) on the India-China Line of Actual Control, 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade and 1959 Dalai Lama entry route; Border Personnel Meeting Point. Requires special DC + Army permit; stark high-altitude terrain.

name: Urgelling Monastery
description: Historic Nyingma monastery and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso (born 1683). Smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, with peaceful atmosphere, ancient inscriptions, and valley views. Founded in the late 15th century.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: Stupa-shaped memorial (Namgyal Chorten) dedicated to Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features engraved names, prayer flags, and daily bugle ceremony; overlooks Tawang valley. Maintained with deep respect.

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso)
description: Scenic high-altitude glacial lake about 17-18 km from Tawang on the Bum La road. Surrounded by snow peaks, meadows, and forests; often frozen in winter. Sacred to local Monpa people and popular for photography and short walks.

name: Jaswant Garh Memorial
description: War memorial and post honoring Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles, who held position for ~72 hours in the 1962 Battle of Nuranang and was awarded Maha Vir Chakra posthumously. Located on NH-13 near Nuranang/Jang; maintained by Army with exhibits.
facts: Honors Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat MVC

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and high-altitude hill town at ~2669-3000 m, gateway to the famous monastery and Himalayan circuit. Monpa cultural center with markets, views of the monastery, and base for exploring passes, lakes, and monasteries. Requires Inner Line Permit.
